args.title: Only treat a quote as field-delimiting at the start of a field
args.body:
File: src/ingest/parser.ts

splitFields currently toggles inQuotes on any `"` character, even mid-field, so a description like `Monitor 27" Dell U2724D` opens an unterminated quoted field and swallows the rest of the line, eventually failing the column-count check. Change splitFields so a `"` only starts a quoted field when it appears at the very start of a field (current === "" and not already inQuotes); elsewhere it should be treated as an ordinary character, matching how real-world unquoted CSV exports use the inch/quote mark inside a field.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

Confirmed: splitFields() toggles inQuotes on every `"` it sees, even one in the middle of an unquoted field like `Monitor 27" Dell U2724D`. That opens a quoted span that never closes, swallowing the rest of the line (including the real commas) until assertShape sees too few columns and throws errors.rowShape. The fix belongs in splitFields: only treat a `"` as starting a quoted field when it's the first character of that field; otherwise treat it as a literal character. Opened a draft PR with that proposed change rather than merging #952 directly, since the fix is best made at the point a quote is recognized (field start) rather than disabling quote-handling altogether.
